cpp-template-inherited-base-signature.item: - The inherited traversal calls `cpp_direct_base_types` (`src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:3023`), which reads `unit.signature()` when present and source text otherwise (`src/analyzer/usages/get_definition.rs:3211`). Class `CodeUnit`s are constructed with `scope.template_signature` as their identity signature, which `CodeUnit::signature` returns (`src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:317`, `src/analyzer/model.rs:355`); inside a template declaration that field is assigned `cpp_template_signature`, the normalized text from the first `<` to the last `>` of the span between the `template` keyword and the start of the declaration child, i.e. the template parameter head; the declaration child (`class_specifier` with its name, base clause and body) begins after that span (`src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:207`, `src/analyzer/cpp/declarations.rs:1317`).
cpp-template-inherited-base-signature.why: The absence 'not the class base clause' is no longer stated; a reader must infer it from the span boundaries and the added claim about where the class_specifier starts. The edit also adds new facts about the span, normalization and the class_specifier layout.
elements_not_kept: absence: the value is not the class base clause
added: cpp_template_signature is the normalized text from the first '<' to the last '>' of the span from the template keyword to the declaration child
added: the field is assigned only inside a template declaration
added: the declaration child (class_specifier with name, base clause and body) begins after that span
added: CodeUnit::signature returns the identity field
